question: What is the main focus of mental health promotion in midwifery?

options.A: Diagnosing rare psychiatric disorders during the first trimester
options.B: Focusing exclusively on physical recovery after childbirth
options.C: Prescribing strong antidepressant medications for all patients
options.D: Enhancing overall emotional well-being and building resilience

explanation: Mental health promotion aims to foster positive psychological health, build coping skills, and support emotional resilience rather than treating diagnosed illnesses. [learn more](BMP223_U1_T5#BMP223_U1_T5_h1)

question: Why are midwives well-positioned to promote mental health in women?

options.A: They have frequent contact with women throughout pregnancy and childbirth
options.B: They manage patients exclusively inside large psychiatric hospitals
options.C: They are the only healthcare workers allowed to give psychiatric drugs
options.D: They receive specialized training in neurosurgery and brain chemistry

explanation: Because midwives see mothers regularly during antenatal and postnatal visits, they have continuous opportunities to observe emotional changes and offer support. [learn more](BMP223_U1_T5#BMP223_U1_T5_h1)

question: Which of these is a core responsibility of a midwife in mental health promotion?

options.A: Forcing families to follow strict psychological treatment plans
options.B: Performing major psychiatric surgeries on postnatal patients
options.C: Educating mothers and families about normal emotional changes
options.D: Isolating depressed mothers from their newborn infants

explanation: Midwives help demystify the postpartum period by teaching mothers and their support systems what emotional changes to expect. [learn more](BMP223_U1_T5#BMP223_U1_T5_h2)

question: A new mother shares that she feels very anxious about caring for her baby. What should the midwife do first?

options.A: Tell her that every mother feels this way and dismiss the concern
options.B: Advise her to stop breastfeeding immediately to reduce stress
options.C: Refer her immediately to an inpatient psychiatric facility
options.D: Listen actively and provide a safe space to discuss her fears

explanation: Active listening validates the mother's feelings and forms the foundation of supportive care before deciding if further intervention is needed. [learn more](BMP223_U1_T5#BMP223_U1_T5_h2)

question: Which tool is commonly used to screen for emotional distress after childbirth?
explanation: The EPDS is a widely recognized, simple questionnaire used by healthcare providers to identify women experiencing perinatal depression and anxiety. [learn more](BMP223_U1_T5#BMP223_U1_T5_h3)

question: Why do we screen for mental health distress during antenatal and postnatal care?

options.A: It replaces the need for physical blood pressure checks in labor
options.B: It allows for early identification and prevents severe complications
options.C: It proves whether the mother will be a good parent in the future
options.D: It is required to discharge the patient from the hospital ward

explanation: Finding signs of distress early means support can be given before symptoms escalate into severe mental health crises. [learn more](BMP223_U1_T5#BMP223_U1_T5_h3)

question: Which communication skill helps a patient share her true feelings most effectively?

options.A: Using closed-ended questions that require only a yes or no
options.B: Giving immediate advice before letting the patient finish speaking
options.C: Asking open-ended questions and practicing active listening
options.D: Interrupting the patient frequently to speed up the clinic visit

explanation: Open-ended questions give patients the freedom to express their thoughts and emotions in their own words, building trust and rapport. [learn more](BMP223_U1_T5#BMP223_U1_T5_h4)

question: What is a major barrier to mental health care in many communities?

options.A: Patients refusing to take any form of medical advice
options.B: The complete absence of pregnancy complications anywhere
options.C: An overabundance of psychiatric doctors in rural clinics
options.D: Social stigma and misconceptions about mental illness

explanation: Stigma and cultural misconceptions often prevent individuals and families from acknowledging mental health issues and seeking proper care. [learn more](BMP223_U1_T5#BMP223_U1_T5_h5)

question: How can midwives help reduce mental health stigma in their communities?

options.A: By ignoring cultural beliefs entirely without any discussion
options.B: By keeping all mental health education strictly inside locked wards
options.C: By punishing families who hide their relatives with mental illness
options.D: By educating community leaders and framing mental health as treatable

explanation: Community education helps replace fear and judgment with understanding, encouraging early reporting and supportive care. [learn more](BMP223_U1_T5#BMP223_U1_T5_h5)

question: When should a midwife refer a patient to a mental health specialist?

options.A: When the patient's psychological needs exceed midwifery scope
options.B: When the midwife wants to avoid talking to the patient
options.C: Whenever the patient attends a routine antenatal checkup
options.D: Only after the patient has completely recovered from childbirth

explanation: Severe conditions like deep depression, psychosis, or thoughts of self-harm require specialist psychiatric care beyond general midwifery support. [learn more](BMP223_U1_T5#BMP223_U1_T5_h6)

question: Which professionals should midwives work with to care for a distressed mother?

options.A: Psychiatric nurses, medical social workers, and clinical psychologists
options.B: Only other junior midwifery students on clinical rotation
options.C: Hospital accountants, security guards, and catering staff
options.D: Pharmaceutical sales representatives and medical equipment vendors

explanation: Holistic mental health care requires a multidisciplinary team approach involving various health and social care professionals. [learn more](BMP223_U1_T5#BMP223_U1_T5_h6)
